results.title: Maritime safety rules before 1914
results.content: Before 1914, the number of lifeboats a British passenger ship carried was set by its tonnage, not by the number of people aboard; ships over 10,000 tons needed 16 boats.

results.title: How lifeboats were loaded
results.content: Crews usually loaded lifeboats by deck and by the officers' orders, and the custom of women and children first was applied unevenly between ships and sides of the deck.

results.title: Transatlantic ports of call
results.content: Cherbourg, in Normandy, France, and Queenstown, now Cobh, in County Cork, Ireland, were the usual calling ports for liners sailing from Southampton to New York.

results.title: Cobh heritage notes
results.content: Queenstown was renamed Cobh in 1920; its harbour was a main emigration port.

results.title: Life aboard an ocean liner
results.content: A first class ticket usually included a private cabin, meals in the main dining saloon, and access to the lounges, libraries and promenade decks of the upper decks.

results.title: Classes of travel on early liners
results.content: Second and third class passengers had their own dining rooms and decks, and fares differed many times over between the classes.

results.title: Online retail returns explained
results.content: Online retailers often report return rates between 20% and 30% of orders, higher than in physical stores.

results.title: What counts as a return
results.content: A return rate is usually the share of units or orders sent back in a period, and retailers differ in whether exchanges count.

results.title: Retail glossary: SKU
results.content: SKU stands for stock keeping unit: a code a retailer gives each distinct product and variant it sells, such as one size and colour of a shirt.

results.title: SKUs and barcodes
results.content: Unlike a UPC barcode, a SKU is internal to one retailer, which defines its own format.

results.title: Net Promoter Score basics
results.content: The Net Promoter Score asks customers how likely they are to recommend a company on a 0 to 10 scale; it is the share of promoters (9-10) minus the share of detractors (0-6).

results.title: Criticism of NPS
results.content: Researchers note that the score compresses answers into three groups and can hide changes in the middle.
